For the case you describe, you can use R code in ui.R to populate the choices for the selectInput or checkboxGroupInput; it's just a normal vector or list object, and how you generate that object is up to you.

For example:
https://gist.github.com/3239667
shiny::runGist(3239667)

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Evaluate Query Results As Input
parts:
In ui.r, you can use uiOutput(), and give it something you construct in server.r.

I've made an example at https://gist.github.com/4211337, and you can see it in action here:
http://glimmer.rstudio.com/winston/dynamic_ui/

Here's the code:

ui.r:
========


# Define UI for miles per gallon application


shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(



  headerPanel(""),






  sidebarPanel(
    uiOutput("choose_dataset"),






    uiOutput("choose_columns")



  ),






  mainPanel(
    tableOutput("data_table")



  )


))


server.r
=======


# Some pre-computed stuff in R. In this example, just assign values to a var



data_sets <- c("mtcars", "morley", "rock")







shinyServer(function(input, output) {






  # Drop-down selection box for which data set


  output$choose_dataset <- reactiveUI(function() {



    selectInput("dataset", "Data set", as.list(data_sets))



  })



  # Check boxes



  output$choose_columns <- reactiveUI(function() {



    # Get the data set with the appropriate name



    dat <- get(input$dataset)



    colnames <- names(dat)






    # Create the checkboxes and select them all by default


    checkboxGroupInput("columns", "Choose columns", 



                        choices  = colnames,



                        selected = colnames)



  })






  # Output the data


  output$data_table <- reactiveTable(function() {



        # Get the data set



        dat <- get(input$dataset)






        # Keep the selected columns


        dat <- dat[, input$columns, drop = FALSE]






        # Return first 20 rows


        head(dat, 20)



  })


})

-Winston
